{"description":"THE QUESTION. The Modern IRC Client Protocol §"RPL_REHASHING (382)"
says 382 is "Sent to an operator which has just successfully issued a
REHASH command", and §"ERR_NOPRIVILEGES (481)", REHASH's only other
numeric, "Indicates that the command failed because the user is not an
IRC operator. The text used in the last param of this message may
vary." mimid has no operator state of any kind: OPER answers 491
ERR_NOOPERHOST (decision mimid-1wgh.141), there is no user mode `o` and
381 RPL_YOUREOPER is never sent. So under the spec's own vocabulary
every mimid client is a non-operator and both numerics are unreachable.

THE TWO READINGS.

(A) No operator, so no REHASH: every REHASH is 481, since the user is
not an operator. Literal, and it throws away the one operator verb a
personal daemon can actually carry out. The epic's own principle
(mimid-1wgh.140, class 3) is that IRC's verb fits the daemon's
operation.

(B) The single authenticated user is this server's operator for this
verb's purpose, so a REHASH that read the file gets 382. Deviates from
382's prose, which expects a state mimid does not keep.

THE CHOICE: (B), which bead mimid-1wgh.140.4 asked for. There is one
user, that user runs this daemon, and asking it to re-read its own file
escalates nothing; the credential checked before registration ended
(docs/design/frontend-auth.md §4.1) is the whole of this boundary's
authorization and REHASH adds none.

WHAT FOLLOWS, and the part that is not free. Having sent 382 to this
client, mimid may not send it 481 for another REHASH, because 481's
condition is "the user is not an IRC operator" and Modern lets that
numeric's text vary, not its condition. So every REHASH that reads
nothing -- no configuration file (a daemon configured in code), a file
that will not parse, a parameter naming another server -- is a NOTICE
and no 382, which is the same shape as a reload that applied nothing.
RESTART keeps its 481 because there the refusal is of the command
itself, on Modern §"RESTART message"'s own sentence that it "is
optional since it may be viewed as a risk".

Recorded in crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/command.rs at the REHASH arm,
the crate's Limitations, and docs/design/agent-frontends.md §7.38."}

Settled from the Modern IRC Client Protocol and the code during mimid-1wgh.140.4: 382 treats the one authenticated user as this server's operator, and no REHASH answers 481. The REHASH arm in command.rs, the crate's Limitations and docs/design/agent-frontends.md §7.38 carry the pointer.
